what_happened: The job was meant to change the commit trailer so a job rejected by a failed check says `Athena-Verifier: none (check fmt failed)` and does not name a verifier model that never ran. It was rejected. The final verdict was "fail: the verifier did not complete: deadline of 1200s reached". All 6 acceptance criteria are listed as unmet: the two athena-core unit tests (the trailer with no verifier invocation, and the `<model> pass` / `<model> fail` trailer when one exists), the cargo test/clippy/fmt gate, the run.rs change, the docs/records.md entry, and the focused-change criterion. No failed checks and no blocker or major findings are listed. The work was not shown to be wrong. The verifier timed out, so none of the criteria were judged.
cause: The verifier runs under one fixed 1200s wall-clock deadline. The deadline does not scale with the cargo build and test work the criteria require (test, clippy and fmt across the workspace). The verifier also has no progress record, no early stop and no resume. A timeout therefore produces the same "fail" verdict as a real defect, with all criteria marked unmet. The system has no "could not verify" outcome. This is related to the earlier verifier-environment case (3r97), but there the environment was broken. Here the verifier ran out of time. It is also related to the producer-deadline class (9ymk), but it happens on the verifier side. The stored fields do not show why it was slow, such as a cold build, contention or a stuck command, so this is an inference.
prevention: Add a distinct "unverified" outcome for a verifier that times out or otherwise cannot finish. It must not be recorded as a rejection of the work. On that outcome, Athena should automatically re-run verification once, reusing the build already done in the snapshot, with a deadline scaled to the work. Running the cargo gate once, ahead of the verifier, and handing its recorded output over would remove the main time cost. The verifier should write each criterion verdict as it reaches it, so a timeout keeps the partial result. The job record and the commit trailer should say "verifier did not complete" instead of listing every criterion as unmet.
proposed_request: Make a verifier timeout a distinct "unverified" outcome and not a rejection of the work. When the verifier hits its deadline before finishing, the job must not be recorded as failed with every criterion unmet. It should be recorded as unverified. Athena should then retry verification once automatically, with the same snapshot and a longer deadline. The verifier should record each criterion verdict as soon as it is reached, so that a timeout keeps the criteria already judged. The commit trailer and the job report should say that the verifier did not complete and name the deadline. They should not say the work failed. Add tests in athena-core. One test checks that a deadline-exceeded verifier produces the unverified outcome and not a fail verdict. One checks that criteria judged before the deadline are kept. One checks that the automatic retry happens once and no more. Document the new outcome in docs/records.md. Make no change to governance files. Then re-run job 20261010-154005-jsdj (the Athena-Verifier `none (check <name> failed)` trailer change) so that it gets a real verdict.
